title: Course registration
response: Sign in to your institution’s student portal and open Course Registration. Select the courses approved for your programme, check prerequisites and credit limits with your adviser, then submit and save your registration slip. If registration is closed or a course is missing, contact your department. Exact steps depend on your institution.
source: General guidance — confirm with your institution

title: Fees & payment
examples: What is the school fee deadline?
response: Check the current fee schedule and payment deadline on your institution’s official portal or with the bursary. Use only approved payment channels and keep your receipt. This demo has no verified fee amounts or deadlines; the 30 March date in the original prototype was an example, not a confirmed institutional deadline.
source: General guidance — confirm with your institution

title: Transcripts
examples: How do I apply for a transcript?
response: Contact the registry or use the official transcript application section of your student portal. You will usually need your student number, destination details and proof of any required payment. Confirm processing time and delivery options with the registry; avoid posting personal records here.
source: General guidance — confirm with your institution

title: Exams & timetable
response: Look for the latest examination timetable on your institution’s official portal or departmental notice board. Confirm the course code, date, time and venue. Report timetable clashes to your department or exams office promptly. This assistant cannot confirm live exam dates.
source: General guidance — confirm with your institution

title: Results & grades
examples: How do I check my results?
response: Open the Results section of your student portal to view published grades. For a missing or disputed result, contact your course lecturer or department using the official review process. Your adviser can explain GPA and progression rules. This assistant cannot access individual student results.
source: General guidance — confirm with your institution

title: Admissions
examples: How do I apply for admission?
response: Use the institution’s official admissions page to check entry requirements, application dates and your application status. Newly admitted students should follow the published acceptance and clearance steps. Confirm requirements with admissions because they vary by programme and session.
source: General guidance — confirm with your institution

title: Accommodation
response: Check the official accommodation application process and availability with student affairs or the housing office. Apply through approved channels and confirm charges before paying. Do not send money to unverified agents.
source: General guidance — confirm with your institution

title: Scholarships
response: Ask student affairs or the financial aid office about available scholarships and bursaries. Check eligibility, required documents and deadlines on official notices. Prepare your academic records and application documents, and verify any external scholarship provider before sharing personal information.
source: General guidance — confirm with your institution

title: Study support
response: Start with a weekly plan: list your courses, break topics into small tasks and schedule short study sessions. Practise past questions, use active recall and review difficult topics regularly. For course-specific help, visit your lecturer, academic adviser or library learning support.
source: General guidance — confirm with your institution

title: Portal help
response: Use the official Forgot Password option on your institution’s portal. If it does not work, contact the ICT help desk through official channels. Never share your password, one-time code or payment credentials in this chat.
source: General guidance — confirm with your institution

title: Speak to support
response: For personal or complex issues, contact the relevant official office: your department for academic matters, bursary for fees, registry for records, ICT for portal access, or student affairs for welfare. This demo does not send messages to staff or create support tickets.
source: General guidance — confirm with your institution

title: Wellbeing
response: You deserve support. Consider speaking with your institution’s counsellor, student affairs office or someone you trust. This assistant is not a counsellor. If you are in immediate danger, contact local emergency services or go to the nearest emergency department.
source: General guidance — confirm with your institution
